selection_history: L1 and both L2 rounds were rejected; no algorithm change was adopted, so core is the final candidate. The T9 matrix quantifies reassign, short-turn and fairness contributions on held-out data. No held-out split was read before this freeze.
checkpoint_selection: lowest mean validation total_cost_core over 100 days; earliest checkpoint on exact tie

held_out.pairing: identical day IDs/scenario hashes and tapes across every arm

cost_weights: core DEFAULT_REWARD for every arm, including fairness_zero: total_cost is the trained objective, total_cost_core is recomputed with core weights

analysis.unit: validation/test day (scenario_seed); model seeds averaged per day before resampling
analysis.claim_rule: improvement claim requires mean delta with CI entirely below zero; ID-only gains do not establish OOD robustness

fixed_wall_clock.accounting: train + periodic validation + checkpoint; setup excluded
fixed_wall_clock.reason_not_a_distinct_contrast: No L1/L2 algorithm change was adopted, so every T9 arm has identical per-step compute. The registered fixed-transition runs' observed wall_time_s is reported as the wall-clock view; a separate wall-clock budget would re-measure the same contrast. Rust throughput gains are reported once, in reports/rust-migration.md and reports/runtime-optimization.md.

reward_wiring_fix.finding: The first L3 matrix run showed fairness_zero identical to core: Kernel/BatchKernel hard-coded RewardConfig::default() and never received run.reward, so the reward ablation was INVALID.
reward_wiring_fix.fix: Added Kernel.set_reward/BatchKernel.set_reward (crates/bus-sim-python/src/lib.rs) and wired run.reward through the Python bridge, environment and batch VecEnv; added native regression test_set_reward_changes_returned_reward.
reward_wiring_fix.revision: All 12 T9 arms were re-run on the single fixed build d6bf1551. Core best validation costs are unchanged, confirming the fix is a no-op for the default reward.
